_about: FIXED INPUTS of the TPU x DRAM-on-logic exploration, as the user gave them (relayed in the Codex thread, 2026-11-24). Units are kept as stated. These are not search axes. Derived values live in consistency_report.json (target_profile.py), never here.
source: user messages of 2026-11-24 quoted in /tmp/npusim_int8_codex_findings.txt ([Codex USER-SUPPLIED TARGET DRAM / FOOTPRINT], [.. FOUR DRAM dies ..], [Codex CONFIRMED TARGET -- FOUR LATERAL DRAM DIES]); 1-high stated to Claude directly on 2026-11-23

topology.description: four DRAM dies bonded directly on ONE logic die, side by side in a 2 x 2 array, one vertical DRAM tier (1-high)

capacity.unit_note: GB as supplied by the user; not converted to GiB and not rounded to a preset

nominal_peak_bandwidth.meaning: theoretical maximum of the interface, not a sustained or measured rate

objective.priority: decode latency (over prefill, and latency over throughput)
objective.first_screen: batch-1 token latency; small batch, context and precision as separately labelled sensitivities
objective.workload: not selected -- any model shape used is a labelled scenario

unknown_do_not_invent: DQ / bond interface width per channel and signalling rate
bank-group, row and column organisation; transaction / burst granularity
read / write sharing of the nominal bandwidth
die coordinates, gaps, keep-outs, bonding arrangement
which logic resources attach to which DRAM die (the four memory-interface domains) and the cross-domain routes
logic process node, usable area budget, power budget, cooling
target model, precision, batch and context
decision_variables_logic_side: SRAM (VMEM) allocation, partition, banking, ports and bandwidth
on-chip feed: staging / NoC link width from the DRAM interface to the MXUs
DMA issue: request size and concurrency
clock only inside an explicit power / thermal and clock-domain model (none yet: fixed)
shared_budget_note: MXUs, SRAM, vector / SFU units, NoC, controllers and interface logic share ONE logic-area budget. No area model or process assumption exists here: every resource-changing point is exploratory, with no physical feasibility or optimality claim.
